definition: R5 defines TFW as an explicit philosophy-to-method-to-reference-framework hierarchy: the philosophy explains why delegated cognition requires human authority and durable continuity; the method requires F1 human purpose/authority, F2 bounded delegation, F3 selected material trace plus result/current state, and F4 authoritative result/continuation; and the reference framework supplies proportional implementations, with assurance scaling separately by risk.
exclusions: Raw transcript-only archives without selected decisions, authority, authoritative result, and continuation summary.
Provenance records without purpose, acceptance or stop responsibility, result selection, and continuation.
Governance registers without a concrete selected task, result, decision, and work-continuation trace.
Implementations missing any of F1 human purpose/authority, F2 bounded delegation, F3 selected material trace and result/current state, or F4 authoritative result/continuation.
Claims that the hierarchy simultaneously establishes TFW as a discipline or methodology.
primary_category_claim: There is no single primary category; TFW is an explicit philosophy -> method -> reference-framework hierarchy whose hierarchy must itself be justified.
ambiguities: The packet asserts that the hierarchy itself must be justified but supplies no criterion or evidence by which that justification should be evaluated.
The boundary between F3 result/current state and F4 authoritative result/continuation is not fully specified, particularly whether result authority belongs exclusively to F4.
The packet says assurance scales separately with risk but does not define minimum assurance evidence or risk thresholds.
